text.p: Conoco Inc said Wednesday it will earn a 50-percent working interest in three exploration blocks operated by Texaco Inc in a high potential trend in Colombia, South America.

Conoco said its agreement, subject to approval by Ecopetrol, the Colombian state oil company, calls for participation in a $60 million effort over the next three years to include seismic acquisition and exploratory drilling.
The three blocks, Puerto Boyaca, Rio Minero and Guaduales, are located in the heart of the Middle Magdalena Basin, the DuPont Co subsidiary said.

It said seismic work is ongoing and the partnership expects to drill two exploration wells later this year. Should a discovery prove commercial, Ecopetrol has the option to acquire a 50-percent interest in development of the project.
Conoco and Texaco have also entered into a five-year area of mutual interest agreement for new exploration ventures onshore Colombia, the company said.
